summary: COSMOCREW is an interactive storytelling website that introduces school-age space fans to the robots NASA has left across the solar system. Instead of dry mission lists, each machine speaks for itself, from the Apollo moon buggies and Surveyor 3 to Sojourner, Viking, Opportunity, Ingenuity, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer and Kepler. Learners filter by Moon, Mars and deep space, then open each crew member to hear its story, see how it worked, discover what science it made possible, and read a surprising fact. An “Explorer Passport” rewards curiosity with a stamp for each story. By linking the engineering of each machine to what humanity learned from it, COSMOCREW turns forgotten hardware into characters young people care about, and shows that finished missions still shape today’s exploration.
details: COSMOCREW is a responsive web experience built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, so it works on phones and school computers without installation. Mission details come from NASA’s NSSDCA and NASA Science mission pages. We turned them into short first-person stories at a reading level suited to young learners, followed by plain explanations of how each machine worked and what it discovered. Design choices include large tap targets, keyboard-friendly dialogs, light and dark themes, and a progress passport that encourages exploring all ten stories. The aim is to build a personal connection with these explorers, and to spark interest in the science that continues today. We prioritised accuracy: the voices are creative, but every number and date is drawn from NASA sources. Future work includes an interactive Moon and Mars map, narrated audio, and more missions.
